subject: Onboarding load sprint & benchmark handoff — FastCommerce
messages:
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@fastcommerce.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Load acceptance criteria + timeline

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the kickoff today — we appreciate Redwood moving quickly. To make sure procurement and our SRE team are aligned: can you share the acceptance criteria and a short checklist for the load run? We expect to ramp our traffic to ~400 requests/sec to the inference endpoint for the catalogue search use case. Key asks from our side:
- Target p95 and p99 latency SLOs
- Allowed error rate during the run
- Typical test cadence (ramp, sustain, soak) and duration
- What artifacts you’ll hand back (raw logs, dashboards, findings)

We'd like to schedule the final acceptance run the week of June 28 if possible.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Lee
Director, Core Platform
FastCommerce

Hi Tim — great to meet you on the call. I’ve attached our proposed load plan (redwood_load_plan_v1.pdf) and below is a compact acceptance checklist so your SRE/procurement folks can sign off quickly. Happy to iterate.

Acceptance checklist (summary)
- Target throughput: sustain 400 RPS (client QPS) for 30 minutes with 10-minute ramp up and 10-minute ramp down
- Success rate: >= 99.9% (<= 0.1% error rate)
- Latency SLOs (at target throughput): p50 < 120 ms, p95 < 350 ms, p99 < 600 ms
- No functional errors (model outputs should not truncation/fail the schema)
- Resource stability: no GPU OOMs, no node restarts during the run
- Observability artifacts: Grafana dashboards, raw request logs (sampled), kube events, and final CSV of aggregated latency percentiles

Test artifacts we will provide after the run:
- load-test-results-YYYYMMDD.csv (latency percentiles, success/error counts, throughput)
- Grafana screenshots for key dashboards (tail latency, CPU/GPU utilization, node pod restarts)
- Short write-up of anomalies and recommended mitigations

Proposed schedule (week of Jun 28)
- Jun 28 10:00–11:00 PT: dry run (10m ramp, 10m sustain at 100 RPS) — internal only to validate mechanics
- Jun 28 13:00–14:00 PT: acceptance run (10m ramp, 30m sustain at 400 RPS, 10m ramp down) — observed by both teams

If that works I’ll loop in Marissa (implementation) and Steph (SRE lead) for runbooks and role assignments.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

- Marissa: test harness + client config (artifact path, seed corpus) ready and validated. Confirm the exact endpoint URL we will point their load generator to.
- Steph: allocate monitoring dashboard viewers, ensure retention window has the relevant metrics, and prepare runbook snippet for incident escalation (thresholds we care about: 5xx rate > 0.1%, GPU memory > 95%).

I’m attaching a short checklist I’ll use to direct the run.

Thanks — Monica

Monica — confirmed. Quick notes:
- Client config: we will use Vegeta with the canonical workload and the FastCommerce seed at s3://fastcommerce/onboarding/seed-2026-06-22.tar.gz. The endpoint for the run will be https://api.redwood-demo.redwood.ai/v1/fastcommerce/catalog-query (TLS, mTLS not required for this run; tokens will be scoped and rotated).
- Harness: logs will be pushed to s3://redwood-tests/FAST-1423/ and a copy of aggregated CSV placed under the drive folder shared with FastCommerce.
- Monitoring: I’ll create a temporary dashboard with panels for p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, GPU utilization, avg token/sec. Retention: 72 hours for full-resolution metrics.

Run roles on Jun 28
- FastCommerce: initiate load generator, verify client-side metrics
- Marissa (Redwood): watch performance metrics, adjust client pacing if jitter observed, collect logs
- Stephanie (Redwood SRE): watch infra alarms and coordinate rollback if node instability occurs
- Monica/Rishi: observer/acceptance sign-off

I’ll run a smoke test on Jun 28 10:00 PT and post the dry-run log.

—Marissa
Staff Software Engineer, Implementation
Redwood Inference

Subject: Jun 28 acceptance run — preliminary results and artifacts

Tim / Rachel — thanks to the teams for a clean run. Attached are the aggregated results and screenshots. Key highlights:

Summary results (acceptance run 2026-06-28 13:00–13:50 PT)
- Target sustain: 400 RPS (10m ramp, 30m sustain, 10m ramp down)
- Observed average throughput: 418 RPS (sustained during the 30m window)
- Success rate: 99.98% (5 failed requests out of ~28M requests)
- Latency percentiles during sustain window: p50 = 110 ms, p95 = 290 ms, p99 = 510 ms
- No GPU OOMs, no node restarts observed

Artifacts attached:
- load-test-results-20260628.csv (aggregated latencies and counts)
- grafana_screenshots_0628.png (tail latency panel, GPU utilization, error rates)

Preliminary assessment: pass vs. the acceptance checklist we shared earlier. The p99 (510 ms) is comfortably under the 600 ms threshold and error rates are well below 0.1%.

Next steps:
1) FastCommerce: confirm acceptance (reply to this thread).
2) Redwood: we’ll produce a short acceptance memo and the final artifact bundle (final-acceptance-note.pdf) and handoff to billing/ops for Dedicated capacity onboarding.

If you’d like a short call to walk through the Grafana panels I’m available at 16:00 PT.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
